title: Barrier to entry in collaborative workflow
text:
Barrier to entry in collaborative workflow

We are now in the “Work From Anywhere” era, where we can work remotely with other colleagues and partners across the globe. As a result - of course - we must adjust the way we work, by staying connected to internet.  There are some jobs that can be done through web-based applications. The barrier to entry for these jobs are not too big, because most of us are used to working with computers through the Graphical User Interface (GUI). Meanwhile, as for students, lecturers and researchers, will often work with git, python, r, markdown, machine learning applications, etc - which mostly use the Command Line Interface (CLI) in the process.  To help with this adaptation and learning process, there are several applications with GUIs (e.g.: Visual Studio Code, RStudio, Jupyter Notebook), in which there is a terminal pane - for executing various custom commands. In addition, most people nowadays have a Google account. Thus, python, markdown and r (all at once) can be learned using Google Colab. With Google Colab, we can share notes and source code with our colleagues very easily. In addition, the notebooks resulted from the learning process will be automatically saved in Google Drive.

title: This is my personal page that the themes customized from Robert Michel’s
text:
I’ve been observing many examples before making my own github page. By far, Michell’s theme suits my purpose. Highly appreciate for showcasing this great work.


This page has three main sections:

blog
projects
lesson


Each has it’s own landing page and _metadata.yml file. Additionally the ejs directory contains a small custom listing template for the main landing page.
I agree with Michell’s idea that some older blog posts should not be rendered; rather, they’re sort of put together with images and text.
Lessons and projects use an <iframe> to source the html file in with an option to make it full screen, which I thought was a neat idea.




More settings and configuration for this theme, check the following resources: 1. Quarto documentation page (https://quarto.org/docs/websites/) 2. Robert Michell’s website (https://robertmitchellv.com/) and his repository (https://github.com/robertmitchellv/robertmitchellv.github.io)

title: The shift in Research and Learning workflow.
text:
The shift in Research and Learning workflow.

In today’s AI era, the workflow in the learning and research process has improved a lot. Previously, research activities tended to be more onsite, where the research team had to go for field observation, collect and store data to a portable storage device, process data and conduct analysis using stand-alone computer, before it could finally be disseminated. But now, a research group can work separately on different locations. The collected data can be stored and shared, so that it can be processed and analysed by other team members elsewhere. 
Under this collaborative workflow, we probably will have to work more often with the command line (terminal/cmd, powershell, bash, etc.); especially during the authentication process to the network, uploading and downloading the data to be distributed, as well as when working with GIT (version control system). In addition, we will also work more often with the python programming language, considering the many applications to help with research data processing developed with the python language, notably: scikit and R - for statistics, markdown - for writing documentation, various apps for image processing and GIS, etc. 
But don’t worry. Currently, all popular search engines (e.g.: google, or bing) already enhanced with AI features. Moreover, we can do the troubleshooting with gemini or copilot, or any other AI assistants. Thus, we will easily find commands that are ready to be copied and pasted into the terminal, or other tutorials and supporting references in various file formats.
There’s no doubt that the shift in this workflow, will accelerate and increase the efficiency of the learning and research process. Therefore, I recommend to undergraduate students (especially those studying science and technology) to accustomed yourself with this environment.
